rac:

Faro's force isn't enough to beat Sevilha's defense outright since archer-vs-archer gives no bonus and the fight ties in defender's favor. I consider combining Badajoz's unit with Faro's to get a decisive archer majority, or targeting Toledo instead where spears would counter its knights—though I'd need a spear-majority force exceeding roughly 5.33 strength after the counter bonus. Given resource constraints at Faro and Badajoz, I'm leaning toward moving Badajoz's garrison into Faro this turn to combine forces before attacking Sevilha next turn.

Route Lisboa's spears through Santarem toward Badajoz — next turn Santarem builds up to roughly 5S1K giving attack 9, scaled to 13.5 with spear majority, enough to overwhelm Toledo's knights once they converge on Badajoz.

rac:
Barcelona has 12 troops to work with against two neighboring regions, both defended at level 3. I'm working out whether sending a knight (attack 4) is enough to overcome a spearman defender, factoring in how combat bonuses apply on each side.

Instead I decide to split the whole army: sending 3 spearmen, 2 archers, and 1 knight (total attack 11) to Tarragona, and 2 spearmen, 2 archers, 2 knights (attack 14) to Girona, both comfortably clearing the defense of 3. That leaves the capital empty, but since the enemy is far away, it should be safe, and with 90 wood and 60 iron I can afford to build 6 more spearmen for 90 wood.

rac:
Checking Faro's archers against Sevilha's archers: attack 14 beats defense 8, a clean win. For Coimbra's spearmen against Porto's archers, the archer counter bonus pushes their defense to 7.5, which beats my attack, so that matchup is a loss — I should look at Santarem instead.

Santarem's spearmen-knight mix gets a counter bonus against Toledo's knights (13.5 vs 8), so routing through Badajoz to Toledo over two turns works well. For Coimbra against Salamanca's knights, waiting to merge in Lisboa's spearmen brings the counter-boosted attack to 10.5, enough to beat their defense of 8, so I'll hold Coimbra and reinforce from Lisboa first.

For builds, I'm planning mostly spearmen production across Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, and Badajoz, with Faro building an archer to deal with Porto, and keeping Evora's existing spearmen in place rather than redirecting them toward Badajoz.

Coimbra's attack on Salamanca looks tighter though—7 spearmen with the 1.5x bonus barely clears the 10 defense, so that one's a closer call.

I'll reinforce by moving Santarém's 2 spearmen to Coimbra first, building up to 9 spearmen before attacking Salamanca next turn for a much safer margin. Separately, Sevilha's archers plus knight can take Córdoba's spearmen thanks to the archer counter bonus, even though losses will be heavy—worth it since Sevilha is interior and safe to leave undefended. For builds, I'm queuing knights at Lisboa, Santarém, Évora, Badajoz, and Faro, plus spearmen at Coimbra to counter the knight threats, while shifting Évora's spearmen toward Badajoz and Lisboa's toward Coimbra as reinforcements, leaving Porto's archers in place for now since they'll need knight support later.

Now I'm checking whether Zaragoza's 3 archers with defense 8 can similarly be overcome with spearmen.

Zaragoza's archer defense would actually counter my spearman majority, giving them the bonus instead, so I'll skip that attack and focus Tarragona's force on Castellon. For Girona versus Huesca's 3 spearmen with defense 8, Girona's mixed force works out to spearmen leading with no counter bonus against the enemy spearmen, giving 14 versus 8—a clean win even though it leaves Girona empty, which is fine since Huesca gets conquered. rac:
I'm weighing attack options from Coimbra: hitting Salamanca's knights with spearmen gives a favorable 1.5x bonus against their defense of 10, while attacking Porto's archers with spearmen is trickier since archers get a defensive edge against spearmen.

Looking at Toledo's spearman-knight mix against Teruel, the combined 1.5x bonus just barely clears the defense of 10, so it's worth the risk despite defense scaling over time. For Cordoba's archer-knight pair against Murcia, the matchup favors the defender's knights too much, so I'll hold off there instead.

I'm planning builds across villages—mostly spearmen since they counter the neutral knights everywhere, with one knight build at Lisboa—and mapping troop movements toward Coimbra to set up a later push on Porto, where knights would counter the archer defenders.

Sending Lisboa's knight and Santarem's knight to Coimbra to mass enough knights for next turn's Porto assault, since 2 knights with the 1.5x bonus clears the 8 defense. Faro's mixed force heads to Badajoz instead of Cordoba, since Murcia really needs spearmen and Sevilha's upcoming spearman builds can cover Cordoba. Evora's knight also moves to Badajoz, consolidating forces there for a later push through Toledo toward Madrid.

rac:
I'm weighing attack options against Zaragoza, which has 8 defense and 3 archers. With Castellon's mixed force, Huesca's small unit, Tarragona's 4 archers, and Barcelona's 3 archers available, I'm checking whether knights would counter the archer defense better, and calculating that an archer attack from Tarragona would only tie the defense, which favors the defender.

Instead I'll move Barcelona's 3 archers to merge with Tarragona's next turn for a combined 7 archers (14 attack vs 8 defense), a clear win. I'm also considering attacking Valencia from Castellon with its spearman/archer/knight mix for 11 attack against 8 defense, though that would leave Castellon vulnerable to Teruel's 4 knights -- a risk I'll accept for now. I'll also queue up archer production in Barcelona and Tarragona and spearmen in Girona, then send Barcelona's 3 archers toward Tarragona while keeping Huesca in place.

rac:
Castellon [18] is an empty enemy village with zero defense, so I could send the knight alone from Teruel for a fast one-turn capture while keeping the spearmen home for defense, though I should consider the enemy might still reinforce it.

I'm weighing attacking Valencia (2 archers, def 5) instead: a knight alone wins 6 vs 5 since knights counter archers, but sending spearmen along would actually hurt since archers counter spearmen. Meanwhile, I'm noting Badajoz's larger force (8 spearmen, 1 archer, 3 knights) and that Salamanca is under attack, which matters for the bigger picture.

With Madrid holding 4 knights (def 10), sending 8 spearmen alone gets a counter bonus and wins 12 vs 10, so I'm planning to split the Badajoz army — spearmen toward Madrid, and the knights plus archer toward the Teruel front to push on Castellon, Valencia, or Zaragoza, routing the knights through Teruel first since they move fast.

Sending 1 knight from Teruel to Castellon now as the quick strike, with Badajoz's 3 knights following as backup reinforcement in case it's contested. Pairing the archer with the spearmen heading to Madrid still gives a solid 15 vs 10 advantage despite the speed penalty.

For Coimbra, I'm sending 2 knights to take Porto's archers (12 vs 8, a clean win) while keeping the spearmen in reserve. Cordoba's small force isn't enough against Murcia's 4 knights (def 10), so I'll hold there and bring up reinforcing spearmen from Sevilha, Faro, and Evora instead.

For builds, I'm allocating most villages toward 2 spearmen where wood allows, upgrading Lisboa and Faro to knights since they have enough wood and iron, and leaving Teruel idle since it has no resources to build with.

rac:
Castellon is undefended but borders enemy Teruel, so that's risky to leave empty. Zaragoza's defense comes to about 8 after bonuses, and attacking with Tarragona's 8 archers gives 16 attack with no counter risk, which wins easily — so I'll send those archers from Tarragona to take Zaragoza, even though that leaves Tarragona exposed.

Huesca's small garrison isn't strong enough to attack Zaragoza either, so I'll leave it defending. For builds: I'm allocating Barcelona's resources toward an archer, Tarragona toward two more archers, and Girona, Huesca, and Castellon each toward spearmen based on their available wood.

rac:
I'm working out the combat math for Castellon: my 3 knights attacking the lone defending spearman, factoring in the spearman's counter bonus against cavalry to see if the adjusted defense of roughly 4.5 still favors my 12 attack strength.

For Valencia, since archers counter spearmen, I rule out Teruel's spearmen as attackers and instead send Cordoba's mixed force to hit Murcia, where the spearman-heavy counter bonus pushes attack to 15 against a defense of 10 — a solid win worth the expected losses.

I plan to send Salamanca's 8 spearmen to Madrid now (12 vs 10 with counter bonus) rather than waiting two turns for Badajoz's reinforcements, and route Coimbra's 8 spearmen and knight through Porto to Vigo, where the counter-boosted attack of 18 overwhelms the defense of 10. Zaragoza's archer-defended 15 will need knights later, and I'm noting Teruel's exposed 2 spearmen against a 6-archer threat as a concern to address.

I decide to reinforce Teruel with Toledo's 2 spearmen and Badajoz's 4, but since archers counter spearmen defensively too, I really want knights there — so I'm routing the idle knights from Lisboa, Faro, and Porto to Teruel, accepting that Porto will be empty since it only borders a now-neutral, non-aggressive Vigo.

For builds, I'm planning knights across most interior cities (Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, Coimbra, Badajoz, Toledo, Sevilha, Cordoba, Faro) since they counter the archers at Zaragoza, while Teruel gets cheaper spearmen or an archer given its lower resources, and Porto/Salamanca sit idle with no production. Castellon has fallen to the enemy, now defended by just 1 archer with defense 3. With Teruel's 6 spearmen at home and reinforcements of 4 spearmen and 2 knights arriving next turn, I'm weighing whether to attack Castellon now with the available force.

If I attack with spearmen against the lone archer, the archer's counter bonus brings their effective defense to 4.5 against my 6 attack — a win, but costly. Attacking Valencia instead looks worse since their 2 archers counter up to 7.5 against my 6. The bigger worry is leaving Teruel undefended: Zaragoza's 6 archers are adjacent and could rush in and take it, since my attack on Teruel's garrison of 15 defense would only face 18 effective attack if they moved first — meaning even holding steady is risky. Reinforcements can't reach in time to help this turn either way, so I need to decide between defending Teruel fully or pushing offensively on Castellon despite the exposure.

For Murcia's attack on Valencia, I'm weighing unit compositions: sending just the knight wins narrowly but likely gets destroyed in the trade; pairing a knight with an archer avoids giving the enemy a counter bonus and wins cleanly 6 vs 5; sending the full stack of spearmen, archer, and knight triggers the archer counter on their side but still wins comfortably at 9 vs 7.5.

I decide to commit everything from Murcia toward Valencia since it opens up the interior provinces, and reinforce with troops pulled from Cordoba and Sevilha. Then I shift attention to Madrid, checking whether Burgos's four spearmen can hold against a mixed force—five spearmen and a knight only tally 9 against their 10, so that attack would fail as currently composed.

Next turn with eight spearmen and an archer joining in, the force grows strong enough (19 vs 10) to take Madrid, and I note Zaragoza is adjacent so I can hold position this turn. For Porto, I confirm the knights at Vigo are weak to a spearmen counter once Coimbra's army arrives, giving an easy 18 vs 10 win. I then plan to funnel all the scattered single-knight garrisons from Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, Coimbra, Faro, Sevilha, Toledo, and Badajoz toward Teruel, since merging reinforcements there lets me launch a stronger knight strike against Zaragoza's archers afterward.

For builds, I'm assigning knights to villages with enough wood and iron (Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, Coimbra, Badajoz, Toledo, Sevilha, Cordoba, Teruel), while Faro, Porto, and Salamanca get spearmen pairs instead since they lack the iron for knights, and Madrid and Murcia build nothing this round. I also plan to send a small mixed force of spearmen and a knight from Cordoba to garrison Murcia afterward.
